## com.mailflow.ai

### AiConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/AiConfig.java` - Spring configuration

Selects the active AI provider based on configuration.

If `mailflow.ai.enabled=false` or no API key is set,
the `NoOpAiContentProvider` is used and AI endpoints return
a clear "not configured" error without breaking anything else.

Public methods: `aiContentProvider(WebClient.Builder webClientBuilder, ObjectMapper objectMapper)`

### AiContentProvider

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/AiContentProvider.java` - Interface

Abstraction over AI content generation providers.

Current implementations:

- `OpenAiContentProvider` — calls OpenAI Chat API

- `NoOpAiContentProvider` — fallback when AI is disabled

### AiGeneratedContent

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/AiGeneratedContent.java` - Data record (DTO)

Content returned by an AI provider after email generation.

Fields: `subject`, `htmlBody`, `plainBody`, `suggestedVariables`

### GeminiContentProvider

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/GeminiContentProvider.java` - Class

Google Gemini (Generative Language API) integration for AI-assisted email
drafting. Uses the {@code models/{model}:generateContent} endpoint with the
API key supplied via the `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable
(never hardcoded).

Design notes:

- Model is asked to return strict JSON (`responseMimeType`).

- Timeouts are bounded; provider/rate-limit errors map to clean HTTP
      errors for the caller.

- Email bodies and the API key are never logged.

Public methods: `generate(String prompt)`, `improve(ImproveEmailRequest request)`, `isAvailable()`

### ImprovedEmail

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/ImprovedEmail.java` - Data record (DTO)

AI-improved email draft returned to the user for review.

The user reviews, optionally edits, then accepts or discards this draft.
Nothing is sent automatically.

Fields: `subject`, `body`

### ImproveEmailRequest

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/ImproveEmailRequest.java` - Data record (DTO)

Request to improve/polish an existing email draft with AI (Option A:
AI-assisted drafting with human review).

Only `subject` and `body` are required. The optional context
fields steer the rewrite. The AI must preserve the user's intended meaning,
factual details, links and calls to action — it must not invent recipient
details, offers, or business facts.

Fields: `subject`, `body`, `purpose`, `audience`, `tone`, `keyPoints`

### NoOpAiContentProvider

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/NoOpAiContentProvider.java` - Class

Fallback AI provider used when AI is disabled or no API key is configured.
The rest of the application works normally without AI — only the AI
endpoints return a clear "not configured" error (HTTP 503).

Public methods: `generate(String prompt)`, `improve(ImproveEmailRequest request)`, `isAvailable()`

### OpenAiContentProvider

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/ai/OpenAiContentProvider.java` - Class

OpenAI Chat API integration for AI email generation.

The prompt instructs the model to return structured JSON so that
subject and body can be split cleanly. The user can edit the output
before using it in a campaign.

Public methods: `generate(String prompt)`, `improve(ImproveEmailRequest request)`, `isAvailable()`

### AuthService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/auth/service/AuthService.java` - Service (business logic)

Sign-up, login and token refresh.

Sign-up creates a new company workspace (organization) with the person as its

### TeamService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/auth/service/TeamService.java` - Service (business logic)

A company Admin manages the people in their own company: list them, add someone
with a role, change a role, disable or re-enable an account. Every operation is
limited to the Admin's organization; users of other companies are reported as
not found.

An Admin cannot change their own role or disable themselves, so a company
always keeps at least one enabled Admin.

Public methods: `list(User admin)`, `add(User admin, CreateTeamMemberRequest request)`, `update(User admin, Long userId, UpdateTeamMemberRequest request)`

## com.mailflow.batch

### BatchJobContext

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/BatchJobContext.java` - Class

Thread-local carrier for the current campaign ID during batch execution.

Spring Batch step-scoped beans cannot easily receive constructor-injected
runtime values, so we use a thread-local populated before the job starts.
It is cleared after the job completes to prevent memory leaks.

Public methods: `setCampaignId(Long id)`, `getCampaignId()`, `clear()`

### CampaignBatchConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignBatchConfig.java` - Spring configuration

Spring Batch configuration for the email campaign processing job.

All step-scoped beans (`@StepScope`) must be defined here (inside
a `@Configuration` class) so that Spring's full CGLIB proxy
interception applies.  Step-scoped beans defined in `@Component`
classes do NOT get the CGLIB proxy treatment and will not have their
constructor arguments late-bound from job parameters.

Pipeline (per campaign):

```text
  campaignItemReader  — paged JPA, reads PENDING/FAILED campaign_recipients
                        while the campaign is RUNNING
      ↓
  campaignItemProcessor — skips items once the campaign isn't RUNNING, checks
                          unsubscribe, personalises template variables
      ↓
  campaignItemWriter  — publishes EmailMessage to RabbitMQ, marks QUEUED
                        (nothing once the campaign isn't RUNNING)
```n
Each stage re-reads the status, so pausing, cancelling or deleting a campaign stops
it; cancelling also stops the job execution through `JobOperator.stop`.

Public methods: `campaignItemReader(("#{jobParameters['campaignId']}")`, `campaignItemProcessor()`, `campaignItemWriter()`, `campaignEmailJob(JpaPagingItemReader<CampaignRecipient> campaignItemReader, CampaignItemProcessor campaignItemProcessor, CampaignItemWriter campaignItemWriter)`, `processRecipientsStep(JpaPagingItemReader<CampaignRecipient> campaignItemReader, CampaignItemProcessor campaignItemProcessor, CampaignItemWriter campaignItemWriter)`

### CampaignItemProcessor

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignItemProcessor.java` - Spring component

Validates and personalises each campaign-recipient record.

This class is *not* annotated with `@Component` — it is
constructed by `CampaignBatchConfig` as a `@Bean @StepScope`
so that Spring Batch's step-scoped lifecycle is correctly applied.

Returns `null` to skip a recipient (Spring Batch filters nulls
from the chunk before the writer sees them). Every skip of an unprocessed row
also marks it SKIPPED, so it leaves the reader's result set (see the paging
note in `CampaignBatchConfig`).

A row without a saved contact is a campaign-only address: the email goes to
the row's snapshot email and is personalised from the snapshot values.

Content: the campaign's own plain-text body when it has one (sent as the
text/plain part, with an HTML part made from the rendered text), otherwise the
template's bodies (`CampaignEmailContent`).

Each item first re-reads the campaign status: once the campaign is no longer
RUNNING (paused, cancelled or deleted), the items the reader had already read for
the current page are not rendered or published. Their rows stay PENDING, like the
rows the reader no longer reads, so a resume picks them up.

Public methods: `process(CampaignRecipient cr)`

### CampaignItemReaderFactory

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignItemReaderFactory.java` - Class

Retained as an empty placeholder so that any references in comments or
documentation still resolve.  The actual reader bean is defined in
`CampaignBatchConfig.campaignItemReader(Long)` so that `@StepScope`
late-binding works correctly through Spring's CGLIB proxy.

This class is intentionally empty and not registered as a Spring bean.

### CampaignItemWriter

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignItemWriter.java` - Spring component

Publishes personalised `EmailMessage`s to RabbitMQ and marks each
campaign-recipient record as `QUEUED`.

Each record is marked QUEUED *before* its message is published, and a
record that is already QUEUED or SENT is not published again. Two runs of the same
campaign can overlap briefly (a pause followed quickly by a resume); the row update
makes the second run wait for the first one's chunk and then skip its rows, so no
address gets two messages. If publishing fails, the chunk transaction rolls the
marks back.

Before a chunk is written the campaign status is read again: a campaign that is
no longer RUNNING (paused, cancelled or deleted while the chunk was processed) gets
nothing published, and its rows stay PENDING.

This class is *not* annotated with `@Component` — it is
constructed by `CampaignBatchConfig` as a `@Bean @StepScope`.

Public methods: `write(Chunk<? extends EmailMessage> chunk)`

### CampaignJobLauncher

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignJobLauncher.java` - Spring component

Launches campaign batch jobs asynchronously so the REST controller
returns immediately without waiting for the entire campaign to finish.
It also finds and stops a campaign's running job executions, using the
`campaignId` job parameter recorded in Spring Batch's metadata.

We wire the Job bean with an explicit constructor (not Lombok) so that
`@Qualifier` is honoured.  Lombok's `@RequiredArgsConstructor`
generates a plain constructor that cannot carry qualifier metadata.

Public methods: `launchCampaignJob(Long campaignId)`, `findRunningExecutions(Long campaignId)`, `stopRunningJobs(Long campaignId)`

### CampaignJobListener

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignJobListener.java` - Spring component

Updates campaign status when a batch job starts and finishes.

`@Transactional` is required on both methods because Spring Batch
job-level listeners do NOT run inside a step transaction — only step-level
callbacks share the step's transaction.

Every change is conditional on the status the job expects: a job starts a
QUEUED campaign, and only a RUNNING campaign becomes COMPLETED, FAILED or PAUSED
when its job ends. A campaign paused or cancelled while its job was running keeps
that status (the reader stops at its next page, see `CampaignBatchConfig`).
Cancelling also stops the execution (`JobOperator.stop`); its STOPPED end
changes only a RUNNING campaign, so CANCELLED is never turned into PAUSED.

Public methods: `beforeJob(JobExecution jobExecution)`, `afterJob(JobExecution jobExecution)`

### CampaignSkipListener

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/batch/CampaignSkipListener.java` - Spring component

Logs items that were skipped by the fault-tolerant step.
Also increments the skip counter — analytics picks this up later.

Public methods: `onSkipInRead(Throwable t)`, `onSkipInProcess(CampaignRecipient item, Throwable t)`, `onSkipInWrite(EmailMessage item, Throwable t)`

## com.mailflow.campaign.dto

### CampaignRequest

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/dto/CampaignRequest.java` - Data record (DTO)

Body of create (POST) and update (PUT) of a campaign.

On update the scalar fields use PUT semantics: each is replaced, so a
`null` optional value clears it. `templateId` `null` keeps the
current template.

@param subject           what recipients see, after personalisation: required, at most
                         998 characters, one line without control characters
                         (`EmailContentRules`)
@param recipientGroupIds on update, `null` keeps the stored groups and an
                         empty list removes them all
@param recipientIds      on update, `null` keeps the stored contacts and an
                         empty list removes them all
@param targetAddresses campaign-only addresses (not saved as contacts), at most
                       10,000. On update, `null` keeps the stored addresses
                       and an empty list removes them all.
@param customBody      the campaign's own plain-text email body, sent instead of the
                       template's bodies; at most 100,000 characters, no control
                       characters except tab and line breaks. Raw HTML is not
                       interpreted: it is sent as text. On create, `null` or a
                       blank value means none (the template's body is used). On
                       update, `null` keeps the stored body, `""` (or any
                       blank value) clears it, and any other value replaces it.

Fields: `name`, `description`, `subject`, `templateId`, `senderName`, `senderEmail`, `replyTo`, `scheduledAt`, `recipientGroupIds`, `recipientIds`, `targetAddresses`, `customBody`

### CampaignResponse

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/dto/CampaignResponse.java` - Data record (DTO)

@param targetAddressCount number of campaign-only addresses; present in every response.
@param targetAddresses    the campaign-only addresses themselves. Only single-campaign
                          responses (get, create, update) include them; the list
                          endpoint omits the field so a page of campaigns stays small.
@param customBody         the campaign's own plain-text email body. Only single-campaign
                          responses (get, create, update) include it, and only when the
                          campaign has one: absent there means the template's body is used.
                          The list endpoint omits it.
@param hasContent         whether the campaign has email content to send: a non-blank
                          custom body, or a non-deleted template with a non-blank HTML or
                          plain-text body. Present in every response (launch requires it).

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/dto/TargetAddress.java` - Data record (DTO)

A campaign-only address: emailed by this campaign without being saved as a contact.

## com.mailflow.campaign.entity

### Campaign

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/entity/Campaign.java` - Database entity - table `campaigns` - company-scoped (`@TenantId`)

An email campaign ties together a template (or its own email body), a set of
recipients, configuration, and tracks all processing metrics.

Optimistic locking (`@Version`) prevents concurrent
status transitions from clobbering each other; it also makes a delete and a
launch or resume of the same campaign exclusive (the later commit fails).

`@DynamicUpdate`: saving the entity writes only the columns that changed.
The send counters are incremented by bulk updates from the email consumer, which
don't change `version`; a full-row update from a pause, resume, cancel or
launch would otherwise write back the counters as they were when the entity was
loaded and lose the increments made meanwhile.

Public methods: `successRate()`, `isRunnable()`, `isPauseable()`, `isCancellable()`, `isSending()`, `isDeleted()`

### CampaignRecipient

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/entity/CampaignRecipient.java` - Database entity - table `campaign_recipients`

Per-recipient delivery state within a campaign.

A row delivers either to a saved contact (`recipient` set) or to a
campaign-only address (`recipient` null). A campaign-only row carries a
snapshot of the address (`snapshot*` fields) that is used to address and
personalise the email; saved-contact rows leave the snapshot empty and use the
contact's current data.

The `idempotencyKey` is a globally unique delivery identifier that
prevents duplicate email sends even if the worker restarts or a message is
redelivered from RabbitMQ. Formats: {@code campaign_{campaignId}_recipient_{recipientId}}
for saved contacts, {@code campaign_{campaignId}_addr_{sha256(email)}} for
campaign-only addresses.

Public methods: `targetEmail()`, `buildIdempotencyKey(Long campaignId, Long recipientId)`, `buildAddressIdempotencyKey(Long campaignId, String email)`

### CampaignStatus

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/entity/CampaignStatus.java` - Enumeration

Full lifecycle of a campaign from creation to completion.

```text
DRAFT → SCHEDULED → QUEUED → RUNNING → COMPLETED
             ↓                  ↓
         CANCELLED           PAUSED → RUNNING
                               ↓
                            FAILED
```n

### CampaignTargetAddress

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/campaign/entity/CampaignTargetAddress.java` - Database entity - table `campaign_target_addresses`

A campaign-only address: an address a campaign emails without it being a saved
contact (typed in, or a new row from an uploaded file). It is stored with the
campaign and never added to the `recipients` table, so other campaigns
can't reuse it. Deleting the campaign (a soft delete) removes these rows
explicitly; the delivery rows of a campaign that was sent keep their own snapshot
of each address as delivery history.

At launch each address is resolved by `CampaignService`: an address that
has since become a saved contact uses that contact and its status, addresses of
deleted contacts and unsubscribed addresses are skipped, and the rest get a
`CampaignRecipient` row with no recipient and a snapshot of these values.

## com.mailflow.common.util

### EmailContentRules

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/common/util/EmailContentRules.java` - Class

Validation rules for a campaign's own email content: the subject and the
plain-text body written in the New Campaign form. The API (Bean Validation on
`CampaignRequest` and on the preview request), the launch check and the
frontend (`frontend/src/lib/campaignContent.ts`) apply the same rules;
`CampaignContentTest` compares the limits and the control characters with
the frontend source.

- Subject: at most {@value #SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH} characters (the RFC 5322 line
      limit) on one line: no CR or LF, which would start a new mail header, and no
      other control character except tab.

- Body: at most {@value #BODY_MAX_LENGTH} characters, no control character
      except tab, CR and LF.

Control characters are those of `Character.isISOControl(char)`: U+0000 to
U+001F and U+007F to U+009F.

Public methods: `isAllowedInSubject(char c)`, `isAllowedInBody(char c)`, `subjectProblem(String subject)`, `bodyProblem(String body)`

### EmailValidator

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/common/util/EmailValidator.java` - Class

Email address normalisation and format validation: the single rule used for
every recipient address (upload preview, bulk create/reuse, lookup, campaign-only
addresses, contact create/update, imports and the unsubscribe list).

Normalising an address trims it, then lower-cases it with `Locale.ROOT`.
Trimming removes, from both ends only, everything `String.trim()` and
`String.strip()` remove plus the characters they miss: the non-breaking
spaces U+00A0, U+2007 and U+202F, and the invisible U+200B (zero-width space),
U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 (word joiner) and U+FEFF (byte-order mark). Characters
inside an address are never removed, so such an address stays invalid.

The frontend applies the same rule (`normalizeEmail` in
`frontend/src/lib/recipientSelection.ts`, same characters) and the same
pattern (`EMAIL_RE`); `EmailValidatorTest` checks that the two patterns
are identical.

Public methods: `isTrimmable(char c)`, `trim(String raw)`, `normalize(String raw)`, `isValid(String email)`, `requireValid(String email)`, `extractAddress(String cell)`

### RabbitMQConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/config/RabbitMQConfig.java` - Spring configuration

RabbitMQ topology:

```text
  email.exchange (direct)
      ├── email.queue            ← main processing queue
      └── email.dead-letter.queue ← permanent failures land here
```n

Messages rejected after max retries are routed to the dead-letter queue
without being requeued, enabling manual inspection and alerting.

### EmailProvider

Abstraction over email delivery providers.

- `DevEmailProvider`  — logs emails to console in development mode

### EmailProviderConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/EmailProviderConfig.java` - Spring configuration

Selects the active `EmailProvider` based on the configured mode.

Set `mailflow.email.mode=development` (default) for console output.
Set `mailflow.email.mode=production` to use real SMTP.

The real SMTP provider is handed the authenticated SMTP username
(from `spring.mail.username` / `SMTP_USERNAME`) so it can force a
Gmail-compatible From address. The username is blank for MailHog, in which
case the campaign's own sender address is used unchanged.

### EmailRequest

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/EmailRequest.java` - Data record (DTO)

### RateLimiterService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/RateLimiterService.java` - Service (business logic)

Token-bucket rate limiter backed by Redis.

Uses an atomic Lua script so increment + check is a single Redis operation,
avoiding race conditions under concurrent workers.

Each campaign has an independent rate-limit window of 60 seconds.
Limit is set by `mailflow.email.rate-limit-per-minute`.

Public methods: `tryAcquire(Long campaignId)`, `getCurrentCount(Long campaignId)`

### SmtpConfigValidator

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/SmtpConfigValidator.java` - Spring component

Validates the SMTP configuration at application startup so that an
incomplete authenticated-SMTP setup (e.g. Gmail selected but credentials
missing) fails fast with a clear message, rather than only surfacing later
when a campaign is launched and every email silently fails.

Validation only applies when:

- `mailflow.email.mode=production` (real SMTP is in use), and

- SMTP authentication is enabled (`SMTP_AUTH=true`).

For the MailHog / local-dev configuration (`SMTP_AUTH=false` or
development mode) no credentials are required and validation is skipped, so
existing local workflows are unaffected.

This performs configuration validation only — it does **not** open an
SMTP connection or send any email.

Public methods: `afterPropertiesSet()`

### SmtpEmailProvider

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/SmtpEmailProvider.java` - Class

SMTP email delivery using Spring's `JavaMailSender`.

Distinguishes permanent from temporary failures:

- Permanent (5xx): wraps in `PermanentEmailException`

- Temporary (4xx, connection timeout): rethrows as-is for retry

**From-address compatibility:** authenticated providers such as Gmail
reject (or silently rewrite) a From header that does not match the
authenticated account. When an authenticated SMTP username is configured
(`authenticatedUsername` non-blank — i.e. Gmail / any SMTP_AUTH=true
setup) the envelope From is forced to that username so the message is
accepted, while the campaign's intended sender is preserved as Reply-To.
For MailHog / un-authenticated SMTP the username is blank, so the campaign's
own sender address is used unchanged (existing behaviour).

Public methods: `send(EmailRequest request)`

### SmtpSslTrustConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/SmtpSslTrustConfig.java` - Spring configuration

Sets `mail.smtp.ssl.trust` only when `SMTP_SSL_TRUST` has a value.

Jakarta Mail treats an empty `mail.smtp.ssl.trust` as "trust no server",
so STARTTLS failed with "Server is not trusted: smtp-relay.brevo.com" when the
property was always set from an empty variable. Without the property, the
certificate is checked against the JVM's trust store as usual.

### UnsubscribeService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/email/UnsubscribeService.java` - Service (business logic)

The unsubscribe list, kept per organization: an address that opts out of one
company's emails can still be emailed by another company. Addresses are normalised
(`EmailValidator.normalize`) before they are stored, looked up or used in a
cache key, so an unsubscribe made with different case or surrounding whitespace
still matches the address used when sending.

Callers pass the organization explicitly: the batch job has no signed-in user,
so it passes the campaign's organization.

Public methods: `isUnsubscribed(Long organizationId, String email)`, `unsubscribe(Long organizationId, String email, String reason, Long campaignId)`, `findByToken(String token)`

## com.mailflow.queue

### EmailConsumer

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/queue/EmailConsumer.java` - Spring component

RabbitMQ consumer that performs the actual email send.

Idempotency: before sending, checks Redis for the idempotency key.
If the key exists the message is a duplicate and is silently acked.

Rate limiting: token bucket via Redis.  If the limit is exceeded a
`RateLimitExceededException` is thrown, which causes the RabbitMQ
retry interceptor to requeue the message after a backoff.

Permanent failures (5xx SMTP rejection) are caught and recorded; the
message is acked so it is not infinitely redelivered.  Temporary failures
propagate up to the retry interceptor.

Campaign status: before sending, the consumer reads the campaign's current
status. A message of a PAUSED campaign is not sent; its record goes back to
PENDING so that resuming publishes it again. A message of a CANCELLED, deleted
(or no longer existing) campaign is not sent; its record is marked SKIPPED with
the reason. A message whose status was read just before a pause, cancel or delete
is still sent.

Public methods: `consume(EmailMessage message)`

### EmailMessage

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/queue/EmailMessage.java` - Data record (DTO)

Immutable message payload published to RabbitMQ for email processing.

The `idempotencyKey` is the globally unique delivery key
(format: {@code campaign_{id}_recipient_{id}}, or {@code campaign_{id}_addr_{sha256}}
for a campaign-only address) used to detect duplicates.
Workers check this key against Redis/DB before sending.

`recipientId` is null for a campaign-only address (no saved contact);
`toAddress` is always set.

Fields: `idempotencyKey`, `campaignId`, `recipientId`, `toAddress`, `senderName`, `senderEmail`, `replyTo`, `subject`, `htmlBody`, `plainBody`, `attachmentIds`, `attemptNumber`, `createdAt`

### PermanentEmailException

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/queue/PermanentEmailException.java` - Exception type

Signals a permanent email delivery failure that should NOT be retried.
Examples: invalid address, permanent SMTP rejection (5xx).

### RateLimitExceededException

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/queue/RateLimitExceededException.java` - Exception type

Thrown when the email rate limit is exceeded.
RabbitMQ treats this as a temporary failure and requeues with backoff.

`status` is one of:

- `VALID`: a new address that is not a saved contact yet.

- `EXISTING`: the address belongs to a saved contact that can be emailed.
      The saved contact (and its stored details) is used; no new contact is created.
      `recipientId` is that contact's ID.

- `SKIPPED`: a valid address that won't be emailed, because it is on the
      unsubscribe list or its saved contact is unsubscribed, bounced or marked
      invalid. `recipientId` is set when it belongs to a saved contact.

- `DUPLICATE`: the address already appeared earlier in the same file.

- `INVALID`: missing or malformed address, no email column, or an
      address that belongs to a deleted contact.

For every status except VALID, `reason` explains the outcome.
`email` (and `fields.email`) is the normalised address when it is
valid, otherwise the value found in the file.
`fields` holds all mapped values (email, name, company, role, …)
so the frontend can render a preview table and later submit the chosen rows.

Fields: `rowNumber`, `email`, `name`, `company`, `status`, `reason`, `fields`, `null`

## com.mailflow.scheduler

### CampaignScheduler

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/scheduler/CampaignScheduler.java` - Spring component

Polls every 30 seconds for SCHEDULED campaigns whose `scheduledAt`
has passed and triggers their launch.

Each launch runs in its own transaction (`CampaignService.launch(Long)`
is `@Transactional`). This method deliberately has no transaction of its
own: with a shared transaction, one failing campaign marked it rollback-only
and rolled back every other launch in the same poll.

Idempotency: the campaign status is changed to QUEUED inside
`CampaignService.launch(Long)` which uses optimistic locking.
Concurrent scheduler instances (e.g. in a multi-pod deployment) will fail
the second update with an optimistic-locking exception and safely skip the
duplicate launch.

Deleted campaigns are never launched: the query leaves them out, and a campaign
deleted after the query is rejected by `launch` (not found, or the version
check fails when the delete commits first).

Public methods: `triggerDueScheduledCampaigns()`

### DemoAccountGuard

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/security/DemoAccountGuard.java` - Spring component

The V3 migration seeds three demo accounts whose passwords are in the README.
On a public deployment (`DEMO_ACCOUNTS_ENABLED=false`) they are disabled at
startup, so nobody can sign in with them. Their seeded data stays in the "Default"
organization and is invisible to every company that signs up.

### JwtAuthFilter

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/security/JwtAuthFilter.java` - Spring component

Extracts a JWT from the `Authorization: Bearer ` header,
validates it, and populates the `SecurityContextHolder`.

Runs once per request via `OncePerRequestFilter`.

### JwtService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/security/JwtService.java` - Service (business logic)

JWT token generation, signing, and validation.

Tokens are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret resolved from
environment variables. The secret must be at least 256 bits (32 chars).

Public methods: `generateAccessToken(UserDetails userDetails)`, `generateRefreshToken(UserDetails userDetails)`, `accessTokenExpirySeconds()`, `extractUsername(String token)`, `extractRoles(String token)`, `extractClaim(String token, Function<Claims, T> resolver)`, `isTokenValid(String token, UserDetails userDetails)`, `isRefreshToken(String token)`

### ProductionSafetyCheck

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/security/ProductionSafetyCheck.java` - Spring component

With the `prod` profile, refuses to start on settings that would make a public
deployment unsafe, and names the variable to fix.

Public methods: `afterPropertiesSet()`

### SecurityConfig

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/security/SecurityConfig.java` - Spring configuration

Spring Security configuration.

Security model:

- Stateless sessions — JWT only, no HTTP session

- CSRF disabled — not needed for stateless REST APIs

- Role-based access on routes and method level (@PreAuthorize)

- No or invalid token on a protected endpoint: 401; signed in without the
      required role: 403

Public endpoints:

- POST /api/auth/**

- GET  /api/unsubscribe/**

- GET  /swagger-ui/**, /v3/api-docs/**

- GET  /actuator/health

Public methods: `securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http)`, `passwordEncoder()`, `authenticationProvider()`, `authenticationManager(AuthenticationConfiguration config)`

## com.mailflow.template.dto

### TemplateContentRenderRequest

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/template/dto/TemplateContentRenderRequest.java` - Data record (DTO)

Request to render content that has not been saved: the Templates page previews a
template while it is created or edited, and the campaign form previews a campaign's
own body. Nothing is persisted.

The limits bound the work of one preview. The subject limit matches
`TemplateRenderRequest`. Each body may have up to 500,000 characters, far
more than a typical HTML email (Gmail clips messages above about 102 KB). The
sample's custom fields follow the limits of a campaign-only address
(`TargetAddress`): at most 50 fields, keys up to 40 and values up to 1,000
characters.

@param subject    subject to render; a blank subject renders as an empty string
@param htmlBody   HTML body to render (optional)
@param plainBody  plain-text body to render (optional)
@param recipient  sample values used to resolve placeholders
@param customBody a campaign's own plain-text body (optional, same limits as on a
                  campaign). When it is not blank it is rendered exactly as a send
                  renders it: `plainBody` is the rendered text and
                  `htmlBody` the HTML part made from it, and the request's
                  `htmlBody` and `plainBody` are not used.

Fields: `subject`, `htmlBody`, `plainBody`, `recipient`, `customBody`

## com.mailflow.template.service

### CampaignEmailContent

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/template/service/CampaignEmailContent.java` - Class

What a campaign email contains, for one recipient: the single code path shared by
the batch pipeline (`CampaignItemProcessor`, real sends) and the preview
(`POST /api/templates/render`), so a preview shows exactly what is sent.

- A campaign with its own body (a non-blank custom body) sends it as plain
      text: the text/plain part is the rendered body, and the text/html part is
      made from the RENDERED text by `.toHtml`, so the placeholder values
      (contact data) are HTML-escaped too.

- Otherwise the template's HTML and plain-text bodies are rendered, as before.

Placeholders are filled by `TemplateEngineService` with the model of
`PersonalizationModel`.

Public methods: `Rendered(String subject, String htmlBody, String plainBody)`, `hasCustomBody(String customBody)`, `render(TemplateEngineService engine, Map<String, Object> model, String subject, String customBody, String templateHtml, String templatePlain)`, `toHtml(String renderedText)`

### PersonalizationModel

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/template/service/PersonalizationModel.java` - Class

Builds the merge-variable model used to personalise an email for one recipient.

This is the single source of truth for which placeholders exist and what
they resolve to. The batch pipeline (`CampaignItemProcessor`) uses it for
real sends and the template render-preview endpoint uses it for previews, so a
preview shows exactly what the recipient will receive.

Exposed keys: standard fields in lower-camel case (`name`, `email`,
`firstName`, `lastName`, `company`, `course`), every custom
field under its own key, capitalised aliases (`Name`, `Email`,
`FirstName`, `LastName`, `Company`, `Course`) and the
extended custom fields `role/Role`, `phone/Phone`,
`location/Location`, `interest/Interest`,
`department/Department`. Missing values resolve to an empty string.

Public methods: `forRecipient(Recipient recipient)`

### TemplateEngineService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/template/service/TemplateEngineService.java` - Service (business logic)

Handles variable substitution in email templates.

Template syntax: {@code {{variableName}}}
which is converted to Freemarker {@code ${variableName}} internally.

The conversion allows templates to be authored in a simpler
Mustache-like syntax while leveraging Freemarker for rendering.

Public methods: `render(String templateContent, Map<String, Object> variables)`, `extractVariables(String templateContent)`, `findMissingVariables(String templateContent, Map<String, Object> variables)`

### TemplateService

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/template/service/TemplateService.java` - Service (business logic)

Public methods: `create(TemplateRequest request)`, `findAll(String search, Pageable pageable)`, `findById(Long id)`, `update(Long id, TemplateRequest request)`, `delete(Long id)`, `preview(Long id, Map<String, String> vars)`, `renderForRecipient(Long id, TemplateRenderRequest request)`, `renderContent(TemplateContentRenderRequest request)`, `getOrThrow(Long id)`, `toResponse(EmailTemplate t)`

## com.mailflow.tenant

### TenantContext

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/tenant/TenantContext.java` - Class

The organization (company workspace) of the signed-in user.

Web requests from a signed-in user are scoped to that user's organization.
Code without a signed-in user (the batch job, the RabbitMQ consumer, the scheduler,
public unsubscribe links) has no organization and runs as the `.ROOT` tenant:
Hibernate does not filter its queries, so that code must scope by the
organization of the campaign it works on.

Public methods: `currentOrganizationId()`, `requireOrganizationId()`, `key(Object id)`

### TenantIdentifierResolver

`src/main/java/com/mailflow/tenant/TenantIdentifierResolver.java` - Class - company-scoped (`@TenantId`)

Tells Hibernate which organization the current session belongs to. Entities with
a `@TenantId` field are then filtered to that organization in every query,
and new rows get it automatically.

Registered by class name through `hibernate.tenant_identifier_resolver` in
application.yml, so it also applies to test slices without Spring component scanning.

Without a signed-in user the session is the `TenantContext.ROOT` tenant:
no filtering, and rows must be given their organization explicitly. Hibernate opens
the request's session after the security filter has authenticated the user (open
session in view), so a signed-in request always gets a filtered session.

Public methods: `resolveCurrentTenantIdentifier()`, `validateExistingCurrentSessions()`, `isRoot(Long tenantId)`
